articles.title: Tonal upgrades its smart weightlifting machine with heavier weights and a better camera
articles.summary: Tonal has launched the Tonal 2. The updated smart home trainer lets users lift up to 250 pounds of weight, comes with an improved camera, and more.
articles.body: Tonal on Wednesday launched the Tonal 2, an upgraded version of its smart in-home strength trainer. Launched in 2018, the Tonal is a wall-mounted strength training machine with electromagnetically adjustable resistance and a touchscreen display. It can monitor lifting form, offer virtual coaching, predict and set the optimal weight for each exercise, and responsively adjust as you lift for a personalized workout. The company also offers on-demand workouts. Along with sporting a new all-black design and chrome accents, the Tonal 2 comes with a host of meaningful internal improvements, including a new adaptive weight system with up to 250 pounds of digital resistance, up from the 200 pounds in the original trainer. The latest version of the trainer now offers drop sets via a software update also available on the Tonal 1, with the option to automatically reduce weight during a set as muscle fatigue builds up. The Tonal 2 also comes with a new “Aero HIIT” mode, which lets you combine cardio and strength training into a single session. Tonal also improved its optional Smart View feature, which uses cameras to watch your form and give real-time coaching cues. On the Tonal 1, Smart View required you to use your phone camera, and used the on-device camera for a second angle in some exercises; on the Tonal 2, it uses the built-in camera, with an option to use your smartphone for a second angle. The company says the camera also can now use AI to “analyze 500 data points per second.” The Tonal 2 is available now, starting at $4,295, not including delivery and installation, plus a $495 “smart accessories bundle” that the company’s website says is “required to unlock the best Tonal experience.” It also requires a $60/month subscription, with a one-year commitment to start. Tonal noted on Instagram it will be introducing a trade-in program for existing Tonal 1 owners looking to upgrade, but didn’t give specifics. Tonal told The Verge the Tonal 2 can be mounted on the original Tonal’s existing wall mount for easier installation.

articles.title: Google’s new gradient icon design is coming to more apps
articles.summary: The looks are softer and more varied.
articles.body: In late 2025, Google started rolling out new icons with a gradient design. Now it seems the new look is coming to the rest of Google’s apps. 9to5Google got its hands on images of the new icons that ditch the uniform circle design that tries to cram in every color of the Google logo. In general, the looks are softer. Corners are rounder, the gradients gently transition from almost pastel to the more saturated Google primary colors. We’ve already seen this new design language show in updated versions of the Google G logo, as well as Gemini, Photos, and Maps. According to 9to5, this represents the presence of AI-powered features. The new icons are more playful, vibrant, and varied, reflecting recent design trends that have moved away from the flat looks of the late 2010s and early 2020s. Google Sheets, Slides, Forms, Sites, and Keep all ditch the portrait-oriented sheet of paper look. Many of them shift to landscape layout, which is much more appropriate — when is the last time you saw a vertical PowerPoint presentation? [Image: Most of the icons feel like an improvement. They’re more visually distinct and often embrace a single color, like Chat, which trades the four-color speech bubble outline for a green blob with a smile inside it that feels reminiscent of the Google Hangouts icon. The one exception is the Keep icon which, personal opinion, looks like hot trash. It’s not clear when the new look icons will start rolling out, but it will probably be sooner than later.

articles.title: Bigg Boss Kannada 13: Wild card entrant Kumari gets evicted after a short stint in the house
articles.summary: Bigg Boss Kannada Season 13 witnessed another eviction during the weekend episode, with wild card entrant Kumari bidding goodbye to the house.
articles.body: Bigg Boss Kannada Season 13 witnessed another eviction during the weekend episode, with wild card entrant Kumari bidding goodbye to the house. Having entered the reality show just a few weeks ago, Kumari's journey came to an end within a short span of almost three weeks, leaving her fellow contestants emotional.This week's elimination process saw seven contestants nominated for eviction: Asiya, Dhanush, Gagan, Jagadeesh, Kiran, Kumari and Prashant. After the elimination proceedings, Kumari was announced as the contestant leaving the house.During her eviction, Kumari got emotional and admitted that she could not live up to the expectations viewers had of her. She acknowledged that she might not have delivered the kind of performance the audience anticipated, making her exit an emotional one.From Agnipareekshe to the Bigg Boss house: Kumari's journeyKumari's journey on Bigg Boss Kannada 13 was particularly special, as she was not a regular celebrity contestant but someone who had already caught the audience's attention through the reality show Agnipareekshe.A 20-year-old from Nanjangud, Kumari made a mark on Agnipareekshe with her straightforward nature and unfiltered way of expressing herself. She reportedly became the first contestant on the platform to receive the green signal from all four judges, making her a popular face among viewers even before entering the Bigg Boss house.Although she did not make it to the final stage of Agnipareekshe, fate had another opportunity waiting for her. Following the exit of Sangeetha Bhat and Modern Mahakavi Manja from Bigg Boss Kannada 13, Kumari was given a second chance to showcase her personality and talent as a wild card entrant.She entered the Bigg Boss house alongside fellow Agnipareekshe contestant Lakshmi during the festive Dasara period. From participating in the initial tasks to gradually finding her place among the housemates, Kumari began a new chapter in her reality television journey.A short journey that left an impressionDespite her relatively short stint, Kumari managed to build connections inside the house. Her innocent demeanour, candid conversations and straightforward approach made her a contestant who stood out in her own way.Her interactions with fellow housemates also brought out an endearing side of her personality. She gradually became part of the household dynamics, and her presence was acknowledged by contestants who shared a warm bond with her.However, the past week proved challenging for Kumari. She was reportedly dealing with health issues, which affected her participation in the tasks. Her limited involvement during this crucial phase may have also affected her journey in the competition.Her eviction was an emotional moment for the housemates, with several contestants visibly affected by her departure. For someone who had entered the show with hopes of making the most of her second opportunity, the journey ended sooner than expected.While Kumari admitted that she could not meet the audience's expectations, her Bigg Boss journey gave her an opportunity to reach a wider audience beyond Agnipareekshe. Though her stint was brief, she leaves the house with a memorable experience and the recognition of having made it to one of Kannada television's biggest reality shows.Get the latest TV News, TV Shows and more. articles.title: The 16GB Raspberry Pi 5 got another ‘unavoidable’ RAM price hike
articles.summary: The 16GB Raspberry Pi 5 got an $80 price hike, bringing it up to $385, due to ongoing shortages of RAM and other components.
articles.body: The Raspberry Pi 5 with 16GB of RAM now costs $385 after an $80 price hike, the latest in a string of increases driven by the ongoing RAM shortage. This configuration launched at $120 and now costs more than triple that price. The 16GB versions of the Raspberry Pi Compute Module 5 also got a $40 price hike and now cost between $375 and $415. According to Raspberry Pi CEO Eben Upton, these price hikes were driven specifically by a lack of “alternative supply” for 16GB DRAM, on top of shortages for other components. Upton says, “Though these increases are unavoidable, we know they are unwelcome news for our customers. We encourage you to make sure you’re not paying for more memory than you need.” Upton suggested using Pis with less memory or older Pi models as alternatives to the pricey 16GB model. Unfortunately, other Raspberry Pi 5 configurations have also gotten more expensive — the 2GB version got a price hike last month. At $385, the 16GB Raspberry Pi 5 is nearing the price of a desktop mini PC. Upton reiterated the company’s plans to reverse the price hikes, saying, “the current memory landscape is difficult but ultimately temporary, and we look forward to rolling back our price increases when memory costs fall once again.”

articles.title: Ninja’s first-ever microwave just replaced two of my kitchen appliances at once | TechCrunch
articles.summary: The Ninja Crispi Microwave stands out for its FusionCrisp technology, which combines the speed of a microwave with the crispy results you'd expect from an air fryer.
articles.body:
I never thought I’d get excited about replacing my microwave, but the Ninja Crispi Microwave and Air Fryer has made a pretty convincing case for ditching two appliances and making room for one. Combining a microwave with a built-in air fryer, it’s designed to speed up everyday cooking, give leftovers their crunch back and, perhaps best of all, free up some valuable kitchen counter space.

Priced at $449.99, it’s certainly not a budget-friendly microwave. But this is no ordinary machine for heating leftover soup. Ninja has paired a 1,000W microwave with a 1,700W air fryer system, powered by its FusionCrisp technology, which combines the speed of microwave cooking with the golden, crispy results you’d typically expect from an air fryer.

Think leftover pizza, chicken tenders, fries, and all those foods that tend to turn sad and soggy in a traditional microwave. Instead, the idea is to get food that’s piping hot and juicy on the inside, with a deliciously crisp, golden finish on the outside. In other words, no more choosing between speed and texture.

Of course, microwave and air fryer combinations aren’t entirely new. Brands such as Smeg have already explored the concept, while plenty of modern microwaves come with a range of additional cooking functions.

What makes the Ninja Crispi Microwave particularly interesting, however, is its FusionCrisp technology, which is designed to bring both cooking methods together rather than simply offering two separate functions. It comes with a 5.5-quart glass cooking dish and a nonstick crisper plate, which sits on top when you want to air fry and crisp up your food.

Another part that makes it stand out is that there isn’t a rotating plate inside, opening up a lot more space to cook more dishes at once.

It’s not just about reheating leftovers. For example, if you want to make a pasta bake, the microwave can cook the pasta, while the air fryer crisps up the cheese on top.

There’s one thing to consider before buying it, though. Measuring 20.3 x 17.56 x 14.1 inches, the microwave is hardly compact. It takes up a fair amount of counter space, so while it could free up room if you’re replacing a separate microwave and air fryer, it’s not necessarily the ideal solution for a small apartment kitchen.

Then there’s the $449.99 price tag. That’s a considerable amount to spend on a microwave, particularly when a basic model can handle everyday reheating for a fraction of the cost. But if you’re someone who regularly reaches for both a microwave and an air fryer, the combination could make a lot more sense.

articles.title: Vivo’s first Pro Max phone proves its Ultra is still in a league of its own
articles.summary: The Vivo X500 Pro Max is a great flagship phone, but a step back from my favorite phone camera.
articles.body: When I declared this spring that Vivo’s X300 Ultra had the best cameras in any phone, two things made it stand out in my mind: its excellent main camera with a narrow 35mm focal length and what remains the most capable ultrawide in any phone worldwide. You won’t find either in the new X500 Pro Max. It has an impressive camera system with world-leading dynamic range and the same great telephoto lens found in the Ultra. But it’s lost a little something of what made its predecessor quite so special. [Product: Vivo X500 Pro Max | The X500 Pro Max is the latest in a trend that’s seen China’s major Android players roll out Pro Max models, including Xiaomi, Oppo, Honor, and now Vivo. The new models close the gap between their previous Pro flagships and camera-centric Ultra models — or, if you prefer to be cynical about it, are an excuse to slap “Max” on the box to better mask RAM-induced price hikes. A little of column A, a little of column B, I suspect. The Pro Max adopts plenty of flagship features found in the older Ultra. It’s the same size, for one, and has a matching 1440p, 144Hz OLED display. It’s got an even bigger battery — 7,800mAh — which breezes through two days of use, with similar 90W wired and 40W wireless charging. Unlike the Ultra it doesn’t use the latest Snapdragon chipset, but its MediaTek Dimensity 9600 Pro delivers roughly comparable performance. It even features the exact same periscope telephoto camera, one of the best in any phone. Then there’s the price: €1,799 (about $2,000) puts this squarely in the ultra-premium bracket. But despite all that, this isn’t a true successor to the X300 Ultra, which is still rumored to see a direct sequel sometime next year. The X500 Pro Max still sits half a step down in Vivo’s hierarchy, and so it would be a little unfair to expect it to match or beat the older Ultra. The problem isn’t that this camera is worse than that phone’s, though, but that it’s much less unique. [Image: [Image: As you’d expect from a step-down model, the 50-megapixel, 1/1.28-inch-type main camera sensor is both smaller and lower resolution than the Ultra’s, impacting its quality. But the newer phone offsets that a little thanks to one edge on the Ultra: It uses Sony’s new Lytia L910 image sensor, which features LOFIC technology that enables a wider 17-stop dynamic range, with the enhancements primarily in the highlights. But the X300 Ultra’s camera wasn’t only notable for technical quality. I loved the fact that it adopted a 35mm focal length, and am disappointed that the Pro Max returns to the same 24mm focal length found on iPhones and countless others. This, like most phones’ main cameras, is a wide-angle in truth. It’s designed to take in as much of a scene as possible, reserving the ultrawide for truly large landscape shots. It’s part of why I’ve taken to stepping back and using the telephoto by default on many phones, enjoying the tighter framing and better bokeh, but that often brings other quality compromises, especially in lower light. A 35mm main camera, by contrast, feels closer to many of the kit and prime lenses you might grab for a regular camera, narrow enough to use for portraits and purposeful framing. It sits more evenly in between the 14mm ultrawide and 85mm telephoto, giving you natural options across the range. You could of course just use the X500 Pro Max’s 24mm main camera and zoom in a little, but then you’re wasting some of the sensor and relying on digital zoom tricks, rather than making the most of the lens’s optics. I’m stubborn about shooting with my cameras’ full focal lengths whenever I can, and you should be too. [Image: The design has a clever trick to mask the depth of the camera island: The body itself slopes up to meet it. If there’s a saving grace to the decision to return to a wider main camera, it’s that it helps make up for the X500 Pro Max’s other shortcoming: a much smaller ultrawide camera sensor. The ethos of the X300 Ultra was that all three lenses should deliver comparable quality. As such, it treated its ultrawide like another main camera, with a large sensor and even optical image stabilization, a rarity on wide lenses. In fact, its sensor is the same size as the X500 Pro Max’s main camera, so a repeat of that feat was never especially likely, but the 1/2.75-inch-type ultrawide in the X500 Pro Max is still a notable step down. Taking the phone to a nighttime Champions League game, there was a clear gap in quality moving from the ultrawide to the other two lenses. Under the bright stadium lights, the ultrawide blew out the white details on the pitch and player kits and left the crowd in comparative darkness. The main and ultrawide were able to bring more detail out of the dimly lit spectators and better handle the highlights on the pitch, without entirely giving up on the contrast that gave the scene its character. [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: It’s important to put these gripes in context: This is a truly excellent camera system for a phone, and still more capable than any you can officially buy in the US. The returning telephoto in particular is exceptional; every lens benefits from Vivo’s naturalistic color-tuning, developed together with Zeiss, and video capabilities include Log recording and 4K at 240fps slow motion. It supports Vivo’s teleconverter lenses too, including a seriously chunky 400mm option. It’s just a shame that the most interesting elements of the Ultra’s camera haven’t trickled down to its first Pro Max too. Strangely, another phone I’ve tested this month feels like it picked up where the X300 Ultra left off: Oppo’s Find X10 Pro Max, a pretty direct rival to this phone. Its triple 200-megapixel camera system still uses a wide-angle main camera, but at least includes a substantially improved ultrawide camera to create that same feeling that each of its three rear lenses is of comparable quality. All I hope now is that when the X500 Ultra rolls around come spring, it builds on the success of the older Ultra, and perhaps finds new ways to make its cameras stand out. After all, if the Pro Max costs €1,799, the Ultra could cost substantially more — and will have its work cut out to prove it’s worth it. Photography by Dominic Preston / The Verge

articles.title: Dollyy Javved on cosmetic enhancements and beauty standards: There’s no shame in accepting it
articles.summary: While celebrities often shy away from admitting to cosmetic procedures, Dollyy Javved, who has been part of shows such as Chhoriyan Chali Gaon and
articles.body: While celebrities often shy away from admitting to cosmetic procedures, Dollyy Javved, who has been part of shows such as Chhoriyan Chali Gaon and Alliance, is candid about her experiences with enhancements, including chin fillers and Botox. She believes there should be greater openness around cosmetic procedures, particularly because public appearances can create unrealistic expectations about natural looks. According to her, being honest about such choices can help people understand that appearance is sometimes the result of treatments and enhancements rather than simply genetics. She says, “What is there to hide? Getting fillers and undergoing cosmetic procedures is normal. It is important for people to know that a lot goes into looking a certain way and that not everything is natural. Some people choose not to disclose their cosmetic enhancements for fear of being trolled, which is why greater acceptance of such choices is necessary. I am open about it because I do not care about trolls. I have always been authentic and do not shy away from discussing these things because I see no shame in them.”Growing up, Dollyy was often told that the scar on her forehead affected her appearance, but she has never viewed it as a flaw. She believes that comments about physical features can influence how people see themselves, particularly during their formative years, when they are still developing confidence and learning to accept their appearance. For her, self-acceptance is not something that happens overnight; it takes time and the ability to look beyond other people's opinions. She recounts, “Since childhood, people have told me that the scar on my forehead is not pretty and that I should get it removed. Personally, I have never seen it as a flaw. Learning to love yourself is a long journey. When you become a teenager, you start nitpicking your flaws, sometimes because others point them out. It is important to tune out such comments and for people to be more compassionate towards others.”On experimenting with fillers and choosing what suits her:Her experience with cosmetic enhancements has also been about discovering what works for her rather than following a particular beauty ideal. She has tried different procedures, but that does not mean she intends to retain every enhancement. Her decision to dissolve her chin fillers, for instance, came after she realised that she preferred her natural facial shape. She also credits her sister, Uorfi, for encouraging her to consider lip fillers, something she had been contemplating for a while. Explaining how she arrived at these choices, Dollyy says, “I had always wanted to try lip fillers because I used to overline my lips excessively, to the point where they looked bad. My sister, Uorfi, suggested fillers, so I decided to try them. I got lip fillers about a year ago and also had Botox injected into my masseter muscles. When I got my lip fillers done, the doctor suggested adding a little chin filler for symmetry. However, after a year, I realised I was happy with my round face, so I got the fillers dissolved.”Get the latest TV News, TV Shows and more. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Join us for the 2026-27 Wisconsin basketball season on the SB Nation app
articles.summary: Our new game chats are perfect for the return of college hoops.
articles.body:
Almost two months ago, we announced the release of our new app, which you can find here or by searching SB Nation in your neighborhood app store. The app is available in North America, and we're working on Europe and the rest of the world as we speak!

Quite a few of you have downloaded it over the past seven weeks and have been using it, but if you are a big college basketball fan, it's also entirely possible a few of you missed it!

The goal with this app was to make it easier to join the community, and specifically comment, read the comments, and make your own posts, as well as keeping all the community posts – articles on the front page, Feed posts from you – front and center.

One of the most exciting new features is the game chat, which some of you may have already test-driven during the preseason. It makes it easier to follow along with the barrage of comments that come during games, and gets to the heart of why so many of you spend time in our community. Faster loading comments and notifications when someone replies to your comments and Feed posts are creating a more fun experience that you're not going to find anywhere else.

We also wanted to elevate the community's contributions by putting your Feed posts inside one stream alongside all the other articles from the site. To that end, more people have seen your posts and more people have commented on them. In fact, we've set single-day commenting records three different times in the last several weeks.

And if you prefer just reading our traditional front page articles, there's an option at the top to do that.

So, thanks for making us part of your routine. If you haven't checked it out, you can get the app for iOS or Android . And if you're not an app user, that's OK! We're glad to have you following along in whatever way makes you most comfortable.

articles.title: Apple’s ‘Ultra’ smart home robot might have to wait until 2028
articles.summary: The Information reports Apple’s rumored smart home robot could be called HomeView Ultra, but is also facing delays that could push its launch back until 2028.
articles.body: Apple has reportedly delayed the launch of its rumored smart home robot until next year at the earliest or possibly even 2028, according to The Information. It says the robot’s hardware “has been finished for around two years,” but that the software isn’t ready. The device’s software team has reportedly pushed to delay the launch and “attempted to strip back some proposed features and focus the product on a few capabilities related to FaceTime and automating home tasks, like switching on a light.” According to The Information, the device is codenamed J595, but former Apple employees predict it will be called the “HomeView Ultra,” taking after the new HomeView smart display that launched last month. The robot might cost significantly more than the HomeView, though, at around $1,000, potentially more depending on price hikes for RAM and other components. Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman said in 2024 that the robot could have a stationary, tabletop design resembling Pixar’s famous lamp. The Information says it will have a 9-inch display that swivels around on a robotic arm, with cameras and sensors for things like following you around during a FaceTime call.

articles.title: In one of the largest deals in tech history, Marvell buys Lumentum for $115B | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Marvell's planned purchase of Lumentum is one of the biggest acquisitions in tech history. And they both have the same strategic investor: Nvidia.
articles.body:
Custom chip designer Marvell has signed a deal to acquire optical chip and networking equipment maker Lumentum in an all-stock deal with an enterprise value of $115 billion (including debt) and an equity value of about $80 billion . Marvell will provide 4.5 shares of its common stock for each share of Lumentum.

This makes the deal one of the biggest acquisitions in tech history. It compares to Microsoft buying Activision Blizzard for $68.7 billion in 2022 and Dell buying EMC for $67 billion in 2016.

Interestingly, the two companies have one major shareholder in common: Nvidia. In March, as part of a multi-year agreement to purchase Lumentum’s advanced laser components, the GPU giant invested $2 billion to support Lumentum’s R&D efforts and fab expansion. Later that same month, Marvell announced that Nvidia invested $2 billion in an effort to beef up Marvell’s optical networking and chips portfolio.

With Lumentum, Marvell says it will become a leader in AI connectivity, with products that range from chips to data centers. The transaction is expected to close in the first half of calendar year 2028, should both companies’ shareholders, and regulators, agree.

articles.title: The Apple Watch Ultra 4 is $100 off, matching its best price to date
articles.summary: The Apple Watch Ultra 4 is $699.99 ($100 off), while Ugreen’s soccer ball-shaped FineTrack2 Bluetooth tracker and Hoto’s Pulse 4-in-1 Cordless Staple Gun are also on sale.
articles.body: The Apple Watch Ultra 4 is the company’s most capable smartwatch. Whether you intend to put its many tracking features to the test, or you simply want the longest battery life of any Apple Watch, it’s currently on sale for $699.99 ($100 off) in multiple colors at Amazon, matching its all-time low price. [Product: Apple Watch Ultra 4 | Powered by Apple’s new S11 chip (also in the Series 12), the Apple Watch Ultra 4 delivers faster performance than the last-gen version, plus a handful of new Apple Intelligence features. Of note, those include Sound Recognition, which alerts you to noises like alarms and doorbells, and the Live Rewind feature that lets you revisit the last 15 seconds of an in-person conversation. An upcoming Siri Recap feature will be able to create summaries of conversations for later reference. This model has broader health and fitness capabilities than previous models, too. Its sensors promise more accurate EKG measurements, while the watch can track your heart rate as often as every five seconds. The new Readiness feature (not available on the Ultra 3 and earlier models) also analyzes your recent activity, sleep quality, and other health metrics to generate a score from zero to 10, helping you determine whether to push yourself or take it easy. On the hardware front, battery life is perhaps the biggest highlight, with Apple promising up to 50 hours on a charge — twice as long as the Series 12. Like its predecessor, this model features Apple’s brightest watch display and a rugged design that’s water-resistant up to 100 meters and IP6X-rated for dust resistance. It also retains conveniences like the second-generation Ultra Wideband chip for Precision Finding, and helpful gesture controls so you can you can perform actions with a double tap or flick of your wrist. Read our hands-on impressions of the Apple Watch Ultra 4. Three more ways to save * Ugreen’s FineTrack2 Bluetooth tracker is on sale for $13.99 at Amazon, just a few cents shy of its best price to date. The soccer ball-shaped tracker stands out with its playful design, but it also offers some useful features including a non-rechargeable battery can last up to seven years. It works with Apple’s expansive Find My network to help you locate misplaced belongings, while its lanyard makes it easy to attach to your keys, bag, or other items. * If you’re looking to spruce up your Apple Watch Ultra or Series smartwatch, a variety of Apple’s official bands are on sale for up to 69 percent off at Woot. The silicone Sport Band is down to $14.99 ($35 off), while the soft, breathable Sport Loop is available for $19.99 ($29 off). You can also grab the rugged Trail Loop for $34.99 ($64 off). * Hoto’s new Pulse 4-in-1 Cordless Staple Gun is on sale for $69.99 ($10 off) at Amazon. The versatile tool can help with repairing stuff, or putting together decorations. It works with four types of staples and nails, letting you switch between them depending on the task, while offering two firing modes. It also features a built-in display that shows battery life and alerts you when you can safely fire the stapler and when it’s time to reload it. The stapler comes with 1,200 fasteners.

articles.title: BMW is taking on Tesla’s FSD with urban driver assist starting in 2027
articles.summary: BMW will roll out SAE Level 2 urban driving assistance in 2027 starting in Germany, bringing navigation-guided turns, lane changes, and roundabouts via OTA updates.
articles.body: BMW says that it will expand its navigation-guided, partially automated driving capabilities into urban environments starting in 2027, launching first in Germany with other markets to follow. The new system can help steer, speed up, and slow down the vehicle on both highways and city streets using its built-in GPS navigation. While driving in town, it can assist with changing lanes, making turns, yielding to other cars, and driving through roundabouts. But as a Level 2 driver assist system, it still requires drivers to keep their eyes on the road and stay ready to take over at any moment. On the highway, BMW will allow drivers to remove their hands from the steering wheel — but on local roads, they’ll need to keep their hands on the wheel. BMW is the latest automaker to commit to releasing a partially autonomous city driving feature to its customers, as the industry races to keep up with Tesla and its Full Self-Driving (FSD) system. BMW, in particular, recently introduced its next-generation Neue Klasse platform, which includes a driver assist system partly powered by Qualcomm’s technology. And with hands-free highway driving now widely available in many mass-market vehicles, the next frontier is a safe and capable city driving feature that rivals FSD. [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: BMW says its system works cooperatively with drivers rather than fighting their control, which means they can steer, brake, or speed up at any point to adjust their driving without shutting the system off. At the same time, the car shows what it sees and what the assistance system is doing right in your line of sight through the heads-up display and in a clear 3D map on the main dashboard screen. The necessary cameras and sensors already come built into models like BMW’s 3 Series, 7 Series, X5, iX3, and iX4. BMW can activate the feature through an over-the-air software update. The system follows new European safety rules that let cars suggest and make automated driving moves on city streets for the first time. BMW says that outside experts have already road-tested the setup and confirmed it meets the technical standards, with final official government approval expected in early 2027. With more cars equipped with partial automation hitting the road, safety researchers are growing increasingly worried about driver attention and the potential for these systems to cause crashes. There is compelling evidence that, regardless of the company, most driver-assist systems are less safe than normal human driving. Drivers tend to develop an overreliance on these systems to drive the car for them — even after a short period of use. And when it’s time to take back control of the vehicle, their reaction times are slower than what’s considered safe. BMW is entering risky territory with the adoption of a Level 2 driving feature. Much like Tesla, the company is emphasizing that drivers remain responsible for the vehicle even while using the partially autonomous system in urban environments. Tesla does the same for its FSD feature, but some customers have successfully argued in court that the company bears some responsibility for crashes when they occur.

articles.title: Meta will end Quest 2 OS updates in 2027
articles.summary: Meta is planning to release the last OS update for its Quest 2 and Quest Pro VR headsets by March 2027. Meta will continue to ship security patches and critical bug fixes through the end of 2027.
articles.body: Meta is planning to release the last OS update for its Quest 2 and Quest Pro VR headsets by March 2027, the company announced today. The last OS update for those devices is planned to be v213, and after that, Meta will continue to ship security patches and critical bug fixes through the end of 2027. Apps that support the Quest 2 or Quest Pro can also be submitted through December 2027, Meta says. Meta is calling the Quest 3 and 3S “now the baseline for Meta VR gamers.” The company is announcing this shift ahead of the planned release of its new VR Glasses, which are set to launch sometime in spring 2027. “Quest 2 and Quest Pro laid the foundation for this platform, and millions of people still play on them,” Meta says. “Quest 3 and Quest 3S give your apps more performance headroom and mixed reality built in, and apps built for them carry forward to Meta VR Glasses, which run on the same OS and SDKs.” Meta launched the Quest 2 in 2020 and the Quest Pro in 2022. It discontinued both products in 2024.

articles.title: Apple set an iPhone sales record even without a new standard iPhone
articles.summary: iPhone revenue jumped 17 percent with Pro-only models during this year’s refresh.
articles.body: Apple had a record-breaking quarter for iPhone sales — despite not releasing a standard model during its latest refresh. In its fourth-quarter earnings report released on Monday, Apple says it earned $57.58 billion in iPhone revenue, a 17 percent jump from the same time last year. The increase in revenue follows the launch of Apple’s iPhone 18 lineup in September, which included a pricier iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max model. The company raised prices across its older models at the same time. Apple also took the wraps off its first folding phone, the iPhone Duo, but its preorder sales aren’t included in this earnings report. Like other device-makers, Apple has been dealing with supply chain constraints and rising memory costs, leading it to raise prices across its products. Meanwhile, Apple only had a “limited” number of iPhone Duos available in store at launch, with some estimated shipment dates extending into 2027. “We saw higher memory costs as compared to the June quarter, and that was partly offset by the benefit of carrying inventory and lower costs on non-memory components,” Apple CEO John Ternus said during an interview with CNBC. Apple reported a 12 percent increase in revenue overall, ballooning to $114.5 billion. Its Mac business grew 24 percent to $10.79 billion, while Apple’s services division, which includes App Store commissions along with subscriptions to services like Apple TV and Apple Music, grew to $31.57 billion. iPad revenue declined 10 percent year over year, with $6.23 billion in sales. Apple shook up other areas of its product lineup with some other major launches over the past several weeks. It made a big push into the smart home space with its first smart home display and a series of video doorbells, security cameras, and door locks, made in collaboration with LG and Schneider Electric. Last week, Apple also revealed a MacBook Pro with a touchscreen — a design choice that its executives famously resisted.

articles.title: Apple is ‘not able to predict’ when it’ll have enough iPhone Duos to go around
articles.summary: Apple CEO John Ternus isn’t sure when the company will have enough iPhone Duos to go around due to supply constraints.
articles.body: Apple CEO John Ternus doesn’t have a timeline for when iPhone Duo supply constraints could lift. During an interview with Reuters, Ternus said the company is “working hard to get it to as many customers as quickly as possible, but at this ​point, we’re not able to predict when supply and demand will be in balance.” Apple launched its first foldable last month for $1,999, featuring a 5.4 outer display and 7.6-inch inner screen. Preorders for the iPhone Duo quickly sold out, with some shipments expected to arrive in 2027. Apple also made a limited number of iPhone Duo models available in-store at launch. In his interview with Reuters, Ternus also addressed reports about cracked screens, saying “a very small percentage” of iPhone Duos were returned for this issue, and that Apple is replacing them. The company has contended with supply chain constraints and rising memory costs for months now. This resulted in price increases across its product lineup, along with higher iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max starting prices. “What we’re seeing with memory pricing right now is unprecedented,” Ternus said during Apple’s Q4 2026 earnings call on Monday. Ternus added that the company expects to see “even higher memory costs” during Apple’s December quarter but notes that this is “partly offset” by recent price increases. Even without a standard iPhone 18 model, Apple reported record-breaking iPhone revenue at $57.58 billion during its fourth quarter.

articles.title: Apple's inventory surges 154% as memory chip costs climb | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Apple says unprecedented memory chip costs will continue to rise, raising questions about future device prices as its inventory climbs to $14.5 billion.
articles.body:
Apple’s stockpiling of inventory, particularly computer memory, continued in its fiscal fourth quarter, according to earnings reported Monday. The company reported that its inventory increased significantly in the quarter, growing from $11.09 billion in Q3 to $14.54 billion in Q4, a jump of 31.1%. Year-over-year, inventory grew 154.3% from $5.72 billion in the fourth quarter of 2025.

Apple’s forecast of a 45% to 46% gross margin in the December quarter was largely attributed to the impact of higher memory costs. The company reported a gross margin of 47.9% for the September quarter.

“What we’re seeing with memory pricing right now is unprecedented,” said Apple CEO John Ternus, speaking to analysts on the call. “As we said earlier in the September quarter, we did see higher memory costs as compared to the June quarter, which were partly offset by the benefit of carrying inventory and lower costs on certain non-memory components.”

He said that the company expected “even higher memory costs” in the December quarter, which would be partially offset by price increases implemented earlier this year on some devices, including Mac and iPad at the end of June and iPhones in September.

Ternus also said that beyond December, Apple expects memory costs “continuing to increase.”

“As we said before, we do believe we’ll see a decreasing benefit from the carry-in inventory on memory over time,” he noted, adding that the company was increasing its purchases of this key component. “As we work to improve supply, our manufacturing purchase obligations have increased by 33 billion dollars from June to the September quarter, which you’ll see in our annual filing when it comes out tomorrow.”

Apple also brought COO Sabih Khan, who oversees the company’s supply chain and manufacturing, onto the call to address questions about memory. He reiterated the increased purchase obligations but did not rule out future price increases on Apple devices.

The company also blamed supply constraints for weak iPad sales in the quarter. The iPad was one of the only product segments that didn’t grow, even as iPhone and Mac sales beat estimates. iPad revenue was $6.2 billion, below analysts’ expectations of $6.7 billion. The figure was also down 10% from the prior year.

articles.title: Apple says it's 'hard to predict' when iPhone Duo constraints will improve | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Apple says iPhone Duo production is ramping up, but it still can't say when supply will catch up with demand as shipping delays stretch into next year.
articles.body:
Apple Chief Operating Officer Sabih Khan acknowledged the shipping delays plaguing the new iPhone Duo during the company’s fiscal fourth-quarter earnings call on Monday, but offered little clarity on when customers can expect relief.

The delays were just one point of concern during an earnings call filled with questions about the rising costs memory chip costs, driven by soaring demand from the AI industry.

“iPhone Duo is constrained as of today. The ramp is going well, and we’re working hard to get this revolutionary new product into the hands of our customers as quickly as possible. But at this time, it’s really hard to predict when supply and demand will be in balance,” Khan said.

Customers who didn’t wait in line at an Apple Store or immediately jump on preorders are now seeing ship times stretch into next year . Meanwhile, Verizon has been apologizing to its customers for the delays by offering gift cards.

In an October report from the Financial Times , Apple described demand for the Duo as “nothing short of extraordinary,” after the device sold out on the company’s website within hours of going on sale, pushing delivery dates into next year.

The prolonged shipping delays are notable given Apple’s reputation for its highly efficient supply chain. But the company is hardly alone in facing suply pressures. Soaring demand for memory chips from the AI industry has driven up component costs for hardware makers across the board, dthreatening to push device prices even higher.

Apple, too, has raised prices on a number of products, Khan noted on the call, adding that those decisions were made “reluctantly.”

In another sign of the company’s efforts to meet demand for the Duo, Apple said it’s “deepening” its partnership with Perryman, a titanium producer for supplying materials for the new foldable device.

“We’ve been thrilled with the early response from reviewers and customers, and we are working hard to get iPhone Duo into customers’ hands as quickly as we can,” Apple CEO John Ternus said during his opening remarks.

articles.title: Ukraine’s new pocket-sized gadget turns Russian drones’ cameras against them | TechCrunch
articles.summary: A Kyiv startup’s pocket-sized, 10-ounce receiver lets Ukrainian troops watch the video feeds of Russian drones, though Russian moves toward digital video and AI-guided drones that emit no signals could make the victory short-lived.
articles.body:
Ukrainian drone teams have a new way to spy on the drones that spy on them. A Kyiv equipment startup called CODE380 has been gaining attention for a pocket-sized receiver, the D·Vision SDR, that picks up live camera video from many Russian drones and shows it on a screen.

Those drones send their video over the air without any scrambling, so anyone with the right receiver can watch along. A Ukrainian unit can see where a drone is heading and what its pilot is aiming at before it hits.

According to Defense News , the device is light, at about 10 ounces, which is less than half the weight of competing Ukrainian models, one of which weighs a couple of pounds.

It also listens on the radio channels Russia’s newer Molniya drones started using for video in June. Serhii “Flash” Beskrestnov, a radio specialist who advises Ukraine’s president, said in a June Facebook post cited by Defense News that “most detectors don’t see these frequencies, or see them poorly.” He warned that putting too much trust in a detector could prove fatal.

Beskrestnov has also warned that digital video could one day replace analog, which would blind receivers like this one. The New York Times reported in August that some Molniyas are AI-guided, using Nvidia chips and emitting no signals .

articles.title: Google Chinese company, partner for Android devices, secretly turned 1.3 million devices into 'spy gadgets'
articles.summary: Google revealed that it has severed ties with one of its Android manufacturing partners after discovering that the company allegedly built a secret
articles.body: Google revealed that it has severed ties with one of its Android manufacturing partners after discovering that the company allegedly built a secret backdoor into more than 1.3 million devices, allowing them to be turned into a massive botnet and used for malicious activities without the knowledge of their owner. According to a report by The Verge, Google identified the manufacturer as Videostrong Co, which is a Shenzhen-based company that produced Android-powered devices. Google said that it has now banned the company from building or selling certified Android devices and from supplying software for them.Devices secretly enrolled into a botnet said GoogleGoogle alleges that Videostrong intentionally developed, deployed and operated a backdoor which enabled the infected devices to be remotely controlled for financial gain. The compromised devices were reportedly used for activities such as ad fraud, data theft and routing unauthorised internet traffic.As per Google’s findings, the company monetised the backdoor by selling access to criminal groups, which then installed additional malware modules on affected devices. Those modules were then used to enrol devices into residential proxy networks, conduct advertising fraud and distribute further malware. Google said that it has disrupted the command-and-control infrastructure which is used to operate the botnet and severed access to millions of compromised devices connected via the scheme.Which devices were affectedThe malware was found built directly into many device models and brands over several years. Most of the affected products were Android TV set-top boxes, but the botnet also infected other Android-based internet-of-things devices, including telehealth devices, karaoke machines and digital signage.Google says malware was intentionally hiddenAccording to Google, Videostrong used obfuscation techniques to conceal the malicious code and prevent easy detection. The malware was reportedly loaded onto devices after users powered them on for the first time, making it difficult for device owners to know their hardware had been compromised.Google said the backdoor and botnet were "intentionally developed, deployed, and operated for financial gain," indicating that the activity was not the result of a software vulnerability accidentally exploited by attackersSecurity review process tightenedIn response to the incident, Google said it has dismantled the backdoor and implemented changes to its device-manufacturer review process. The company has also terminated its relationship with Videostrong and barred the manufacturer from participating in the certified Android ecosystem.The case highlights growing concerns around supply-chain security in connected devices, particularly as Android-powered hardware expands beyond smartphones into televisions, healthcare products and other internet-connected consumer and business equipment.You use AI every day. articles.title: Google takes Dreambeans to India in bid to bring AI-generated personal stories to the masses | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Google's Dreambeans, its latest AI experiment, now supports 13 Indian languages.
articles.body:
Google has launched its experimental AI app Dreambeans in India, its first market outside the U.S., as the company looks to tap the world’s second-largest internet market to bring personalized visual stories drawn from users’ digital activity to a broader audience.

On Monday, Google expanded Dreambeans, available on Android and iOS, to India with support for 13 local languages, including Hindi, Punjabi, Tamil, Telugu, and Bengali, alongside English. The launch comes less than two months after Google made the app available to all eligible U.S. users aged 18 and older.

Introduced in June, Google’s Dreambeans uses information from connected Google services, including Calendar, Gemini, Gmail, Photos, Search, and YouTube, to proactively generate personalized, illustrated stories about users’ interests and everyday lives, without requiring them to enter a prompt. The app initially featured static, AI-generated illustrations, but Google recently added a feature that uses its Veo video-generation model to even animate images in select stories.

Google said it chose India as Dreambeans’ first international market because of strong interest from Indian users seeking access to the app and the widespread use of its services in the country. India stood out for its high overlap of users across Gemini, Gmail, and Google Photos, Google product manager Gozde Oznur said during a press briefing.

Dreambeans has recorded nearly 55,000 downloads in the U.S. since its June debut, according to estimates from market intelligence firm Sensor Tower shared with TechCrunch. About 63% of those downloads came in September, when Google opened the app to all eligible U.S. users aged 18 and older. However, downloads dropped 84% month over month to about 5,500 in October.

In the first 30 days after Google opened Dreambeans to all eligible U.S. users, the app recorded an estimated 29,000 downloads, compared with 7.4 million for Meta’s Muse, 2.8 million for ChatGPT, 362,000 for Grok Bot, and 155,000 for Claude during their respective first 30 days after launch, Sensor Tower estimates show. However, unlike those general-purpose AI apps, Dreambeans focuses on generating personalized stories instead of responding to a broad range of user queries.

Even though Dreambeans supports many widely spoken Indian languages, users can select only one language at a time for their generated stories. The app can draw on information across Google services in multiple languages, but it cannot currently generate stories that mix languages, Oznur said during the briefing.

That could limit Dreambeans’ appeal in India, where many people regularly switch between languages, including Hindi and English, often mixing the two in what is commonly known as Hinglish.

Dreambeans’ dependence on information from users’ Google accounts also raises questions about privacy and data access. The app uses Google’s Personal Intelligence technology to draw on connected services and personalize its AI-generated stories. Those services can contain sensitive personal information that some users may not want to share with an AI app just to receive personalized content.

Users can choose which Google services to connect to Dreambeans and disconnect them at any time, Oznur said. They can also delete their Dreambeans data from within the app. Moreover, Oznur asserted that information deleted from the underlying connected services is also removed from Dreambeans’ personalization system.

Users, Oznur said, can tell Dreambeans to avoid certain subjects, including business-related information, and the app will try to adjust its stories accordingly. She added that Dreambeans is available only to personal Gmail account holders, not enterprise users, and that generated stories are visible only to the account holder.

Dreambeans’ proactive approach also carries the risk of surfacing memories that users may find upsetting. Oznur acknowledged that Dreambeans could generate stories involving people who have died, for instance. She said users can tell the app to stop showing certain subjects, comparing the feature to controls in Google Photos that let users limit which memories appear.

Oznur told reporters that Google is exploring ways to make Dreambeans more actionable, moving beyond personalized stories and recommendations to help users act on the app’s suggestions.

articles.title: John Ternus’ first earnings as Apple CEO: iPhone sales are up, Mac has its best year ever, but ever-so expensive memory is a worry for Apple’s holiday quarter
articles.summary: John Ternus’ first report card as Apple CEO beats Wall Street’s numbers, but the holiday quarter looks pricier to deliver.
articles.body: John Ternus’ first report card as Apple CEO beats Wall Street’s numbers, but the holiday quarter looks pricier to deliver. Apple’s revenue for the September quarter, the fourth of fiscal 2026, was $114.5 billion, up 12 percent and ahead of the $113.4 billion analysts expected. Earnings per share rose 14 percent to $2.10.The good mood lasted until Apple started talking about December. It expects gross margin of 45 to 46 percent, down from 47.9 percent, because memory chips keep getting more expensive, and it guided services growth at 8 to 9 percent, below what analysts wanted. Shares barely moved after the results, fell about 4 percent while the call was on, and settled around 2 percent lower.Ternus took over from Tim Cook on September 1, so this was his first call with analysts, and he did not do it alone. CFO Kevan Parekh was there, and so was COO Sabih Khan, a rare face on an Apple earnings call. Apple closed fiscal 2026 with record revenue of $478.8 billion, up 15 percent, and earnings per share of $8.98.iPhone sales hit a September-quarter record without a standard iPhone 18iPhone revenue came in at $57.58 billion, up 17 percent and about $1 billion above estimates. Apple got there with only the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max as new models, while the iPhone 17, iPhone Air and 17e filled out the lower end.So where was the standard iPhone 18? Ternus was asked exactly that and sidestepped it, saying Apple does not comment on future roadmaps.Apple also set September-quarter records for people upgrading their iPhones in the US, mainland China and India.iPhone Duo demand is running well ahead of supplyApple’s first foldable went on sale in October, so none of its sales show up in these results. It still took up much of the call. The Duo sold out online within hours, and delivery dates now stretch into next year. If you did not queue up on day one, you are waiting.Khan told analysts the Duo is “constrained as of today” and that it is hard to predict when supply and demand will balance. Ternus added that a very small percentage of units have come back over display issues, and Apple is replacing them. To widen supply, Apple is deepening its partnership with Perryman, the US titanium producer now supplying the phone.Siri AI costs money to run, so usage limits are comingApple rolled out Siri AI in beta for US English users in September and added French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese and Spanish in October. On-device requests cost Apple almost nothing, Parekh said, but server-side requests carry inference costs that land in services cost of sales.Ternus said features that rely on server-side models, including Siri AI and intelligent photo editing, will have usage caps. People who need more will be able to buy expanded access, tied to iCloud+ plans. Apple has not shared pricing or the caps for each plan yet. Ternus also pitched privacy as Apple’s edge, noting that even Apple cannot see the personal data Siri taps into.Memory costs are now the biggest drag on Apple’s marginsTernus called current memory pricing “unprecedented.” The 47.9 percent gross margin carried a boost of roughly one percentage point from tariff refunds. Strip that out and margin fell about a point from the June quarter, a drop Apple attributes entirely to memory.It gets harder from here. Parekh said memory costs will keep rising beyond December. Apple raised Mac and iPad prices at the end of June and iPhone prices in September, a move Parekh described as reluctant, and its manufacturing purchase obligations rose by $33 billion in the quarter.The December quarter will feel it. Mac and iPad supply will stay tight because of memory, with demand running higher than Apple expected.Services set a record, but growth is set to coolServices revenue rose 10 percent to $31.57 billion, an all-time high and in line with estimates. The App Store drew nearly a billion average weekly visitors, a record, and Apple now counts more than 1.5 billion paid subscriptions.The guidance is where it cools. Apple expects services growth of 8 to 9 percent in the December quarter, below the roughly 11 percent analysts expected. Parekh pointed to currency headwinds, third-party licensing, weak mobile gaming and a US court ruling that affects link-out transactions on the App Store.Mac had its best year everMac revenue rose 24 percent to $10.79 billion, driven by the MacBook Neo and MacBook Pro, and Apple says it has never sold more Macs in a fiscal year. Full-year Mac revenue came to $37.9 billion, up from $33.7 billion. Apple also set a September-quarter record for people new to the Mac.The touchscreen MacBook Pro was only introduced last week, so it is not part of these numbers. Asked whether touch means iOS and macOS are heading toward one operating system, Ternus said no fundamentally different changes are planned, and that Apple would not talk about them anyway.Not every product kept up. iPad slipped 10 percent to $6.23 billion and wearables fell 8 percent to $8.3 billion, both against tough comparisons with last year’s product releases.India keeps setting records for AppleIndia set an all-time revenue record for Apple, with the Mac also hitting all-time highs there. Apple Pay recently went live in the country with Axis Bank, which Ternus cited as an example of where services can still grow.Greater China told a more mixed story. Revenue grew 21 percent to $17.54 billion, a quarterly record, but that was about $1 billion short of what analysts had estimated. Parekh said supply constraints played a part.So Ternus walks into the holiday quarter with record sales behind him and memory costs ahead. Apple expects December to be its biggest quarter ever, with revenue up 7 to 10 percent, but higher chip prices will trim gross margin to 45 to 46 percent, and Mac, iPad and iPhone Duo supply will stay tight while demand runs ahead.You use AI every day. articles.title: Sa Re Ga Ma Pa Keralam Li’l Champs: Singer Srinivas surprises Avani with a special gift; watch video
articles.summary: Singer Avani S. S. has shared a heartwarming moment from the sets of Sa Re Ga Ma Pa Keralam Li’l Champs, featuring singer Srinivas.
articles.body: Singer Avani S. S. has shared a heartwarming moment from the sets of Sa Re Ga Ma Pa Keralam Li’l Champs, featuring singer Srinivas. In a video she recently posted on social media, the veteran singer gives her a pair of in-ear earphones during a break in the shoot. The gesture caught Avani completely off guard, and she later opened up about how much it meant to her and how much she admires him.In the video, Srinivas hands a parcel to Avani, who looks surprised as she accepts it. He then opens the package and shows her the earphones. Avani tries them on and thanks him for the thoughtful gift. The clip offers a glimpse of the warm bond the two share on the sets of the reality show.Sharing the video, Avani wrote about how unexpected the gesture was and said that it was neither planned nor scripted. "How can a man be like this? So much kindness, respect, acceptance, and love... I still cannot process the moment when he gave me his newly arrived in-ear earphones. It was neither scripted nor pre-planned. During a break in the shoot, he came over to me and handed me a parcel. I really regret not capturing that moment on video. At the time, I suppose I was just in a daze," she wrote.Avani also spoke about her admiration for Srinivas, calling him an inspiration both as an artist and as a person. "You are such a remarkable human being, sir. You are a man full of wonderful life lessons, and I truly admire you. Every moment I spend watching you, both as a human being and as an artist, I learn so much. The most beautiful part is how deeply you inspire me," she added.Avani went on to thank the singer for setting an example as an artist who respects and accepts everyone.For the unversed, Avani S. S. was a contestant on the first season of Sa Re Ga Ma Pa Keralam Li’l Champs, where she finished as the first runner-up. She has now returned to the show as a Grand Jury member in its 2026 edition, sharing the platform with established singers and musicians, including judges such as playback singers Sujatha Mohan, Binni Krishnakumar and Srinivas, with Jeeva hosting.Get the latest TV News, TV Shows and more.
